transcript: here are the top 10 longest Theatre productions I've ever seen and the way I'm doing this is runtime per ticket so I'm not including any shows that require you to buy tickets to two separate parts in 10th place the 2018 Broadway revival of Eugene O'Neill's The Iceman Cometh starring Denzel Washington and Austin Butler clocking in at 3h55m minutes which included 2 regular intermissions plus a short pause (and that's the 10th place one!) in 9th place was the 2017 Public Theater production of Hamlet starring Oscar Isaac, Keegan-Michael Key, that's Peter Friedman and Gayle Rankin back there and despite the publicly listed run time of 3h45m my performance ran 4h05m including 2 intermissions in 8th place was Ivo Van Hove's stage version of Ayn Rand’s The Fountainhead which also ran 4h05m but with only 1 intermission and may I just say it felt longer this show was awful 7th place was a Kabuki theatre program I saw in Tokyo this was a double bill so two plays performed back to back but you only had to buy one ticket, which is why I count it the program totaled 4h35m including 1 regular intermission and one 30 minute intermission next I'm putting Taylor Mac’s Bark of millions in 6th place at 4h15m it was technically shorter than the Kabuki program but I'm giving it a higher spot because there was actually no intermission but we were explicitly told to feel free to come and go as we please in 5 place I have a different production of The Iceman Cometh this one played at BAM in 2015 starring Nathan Lane and Brian Dennehy it clocked in at 4h45m including 3 full intermissions about 50 minutes longer than the 2018 revival in 4tb place another experience from Japan when I was in Kyoto I went to a Noh program that was 5h10m including 2 intermissions and that was a quadruple bill it was 3 longer plays and 1 shorter play before I give you my top 3 tell me in the comments the longest show you've ever seen on one bill and did anyone see Taylor Mac's 24 hour show? because spoiler alert, it's not on this list I wish I'd seen it! in 3rd place, the newest addition to this list Initiative, which is playing right now at the Public this is a new coming of age play with a D&D component which at my performance clocked in at 5h20m including 2 intermissions in 2nd place another Ivo Van Hove joint Roman Tragedies technically a triple bill of 3 Shakespeare plays back to back but they're all conceptually tied together this one was 6h with 8 short pauses which ranged from 2 minutes to 10 minutes but likewise the audience was allowed to move around as much as we wanted we could even go up and sit on stage but as some of you might have guessed first place goes to Gatz by Elevator Repair Service where they perform the entirety of The Great Gatsby word for word the performance I attended in 2019 clocked in at 8h15m with 2 regular intermissions and one 90 minute dinner break but even if they removed the break it would still have run longer than Roman tragedies so there's no question that it holds my number one spot
classificationReason: A top-10 list of the longest theatre productions the creator has ever seen — multiple shows, no single focus.
